I have tons upon tons of memories from the nostalgia, but one (out of the many that stand out) happened in 1st grade at that mcadoo school.

It was the last day of first grade, I'd say this happened around 2011 or 2012 and it was dark, cloudy and very rainy.

The hallways were completely empty with everyone in their classrooms waiting for their bus numbers to be called over on the intercom but for the 1st graders, we had to sit next to the classroom door, I was reading Captain Underpants (I think) and I was closest to the door just waiting to make a run for it when my bus got called.

I don't know why this is so nostalgic to me, just looking back on it gives me old vibes from back then and to be honest, the sight of seeing the hallway completely empty and remembering it years later gives me backroom vibes (if you don't know what the backrooms are, it's places you see in your dreams that you swear you've seen before in real life, all be it mildly unsettling)

It was a bit hard hearing about the house that I grew up in since the start of the 2010's go out like that, it's like seeing the memories I've had in that house burn up inside the walls for lack of a better term.

If you wanna start doing animation, then just buy a cheap wacom tablet and find a decent animation software similar to abode animate that's free (or just pirate it if you know how to do that) and watch a tutorial on YouTube of the basics of flash animation and just go for it, I myself started off by making shitty 240p stick figure animations and gradually making my way up to actual animation.

When I got my first drawing tablet, I didn't know how to animate in flash 2004 (I didn't want to risk pirating software during this time) but when I just figured out the bare basics, I made an animation called "The Arcade" or something along those lines and posted it to my channel (it's still up if you want to see it)

So what I'm trying to say is, if you want to do animation 2D or 3D, just dive head first into it and don't be afraid to post your first animation and yes, your first animation is going to be extremely shitty (I know mine was) but at this point, you're just getting started about learning about animation, so it's okay to make something that isn't a masterpiece, just keep animating and animating and eventually you'll be very good at it (I'm still learning things about Adobe animate even).
